newsitem.title: ITALY: Castro delayed at food summit by bad weather.
newsitem.headline: Castro delayed at food summit by bad weather.

text.p: Bad weather in Cuba prevented President Fidel Castro from flying to Rome to attend the U.N.-sponsored World Food Summit on Friday but officials said they expected him to arrive early on Saturday.

"He's not coming today. He hasn't been able to take off because of weather conditions. This is what we have been told," said Christine Graves, a spokeswoman for the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO).
"We assume it's the fog," Graves said.

Another FAO official said the veteran communist leader, who had been due to arrive early on Friday and to address the summit at around 1300 GMT, would now arrive "around midnight" and would make his speech on Saturday.
Castro's rare trip to Europe has been widely expected to include what would be an historic meeting with Pope John Paul though no details have been released by the Vatican.

The 70-year-old president, who has been named as one of six summit vice-chairmen, had also been scheduled to meet Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro and Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini for talks on Friday.
Dini told a news conference that bad weather in the Caribbean had prevented Castro from leaving according to plan.
"Castro hasn't arrived yet," Dini said. "He will be in Rome, he will arrive maybe tonight or tomorrow."
Cuba traditionally withholds information on his movements and an embassy official in Rome would make no comment on whether he would come or not.
The summit ends on Sunday when Castro is expected to attend the final news conference in his role as a vice-chairman.
